name: Starter: Chinese
about: Chinese word order in real, everyday sentences: when and where before the verb, and the little words that make questions and the past.

words.很: very; often just makes a plain adjective statement
words.在: to be at or in; at, in; (doing) now
words.呢: (marks a follow-up: what about …? where is …?)
words.着: (after a verb) marks an ongoing state

xiexie.about: Thanks to someone; 谢谢 alone says it too.

concept.line: In a simple action sentence, the subject comes before the verb and its object after it: 我喝茶, I drink tea.
A number, 这 or 几 takes a measure word before the noun: 一个人, one person; 两张票, two tickets; 这个, this one.
的 joins a describer or an owner to a noun: 我的书, my book.
是 joins two nouns: 我是学生, I'm a student.
和 joins nouns: 茶和咖啡, tea and coffee.
在 with a place goes before the verb it happens at: 我在家吃饭, I eat at home.
